answer: Port scanning is a reconnaissance technique used to determine the status of ports on remote systems. It involves sending requests to various ports to identify which ones are open and listening for communication. This is relevant for both TCP and UDP networking, as every service or application typically has a port open for network communications. Adversaries may use port scanning to discover services running on remote hosts and local network devices, which could potentially be vulnerable to exploitation [Source 1][Source 2].
